To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the biological activity of tocotrienols and tocopherols was measured by the rat resorbtion-gestation test and (2) the calculated vitamin E activity after determination of tocopherols and toco-trienols in foods and feeds agreed with that measured by the resorbtion test.
the biological activity of vitamin E is determined by the alpha-tocopherols and that the biological activity varies with the isomer.

the biological activities of the tocopherol homologs and the tocotrienols are different and that the biological activities should be taken into account when determining the vitamin E content of foods and feeds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological activity of vitamin E and related compounds and natural materials.
the determination of the vitamin content of foods and feeds.

the biological activity of vitamin E in the rat resorption test, the chemical determination of vitamin E activity in food, and the chemical determination of the natural tocopherols in foods and feeds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biological activity of alpha-tocotrienols in the rat resorption- gestation test is 13% of that of alpha-tocopheryl esters.

the biological activity of alpha-tocopheryl esters is higher than that of the free alpha-tocopherols, and the biological activity of beta-, gamma- and delta-tocopherols and tocopherols are considerably lower.
the biological activities of the tocopherol homologs are not identical, and that the biological activity of a given homolog is not identical with the biological activity of its corresponding acetate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it seems reasonable to assume that the tocopherol content is a good indicator of the vitamin E potency of foods, but that the tocotrienol content should be taken into consideration when dealing with mixed feeds.

the vitamin E content of food and feeds is not a constant value, as is generally believed, but is a variable value depending on the composition of the tocopherol fraction, which in turn depends on the origin of the food and feed.
it is possible to calculate the vitamin activity of a food from the chemical determination of its tocopherol and tocotrienol content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biological activity of vitamin E is not only dependent on the chemical structure but also on the chemical environment of the compound.
the tocotrienols have little to no biological activity, and that alpha-tocopherols are the most important form of vitamin E in terms of biological activity.
the tocopherols are not the only active compounds in foods and feeds that are rich in vitamin E.
